# AGENTS.md — GitHub Actions

This fork automatically runs only [deploy-image](workflows/deploy-image.yml), on relevant master pushes. It builds and validates the Linux deployment image on Ubuntu before publishing to GHCR. Upstream workflows retain manual and reusable entrypoints only; event-dependent upstream jobs may skip or require adaptation when dispatched manually. Preserve that restriction when importing upstream changes.

Run jobs on Windows runners (`windows-*` labels) under native `pwsh`. Retain the separate native Windows jobs in `ci-windows.yml` and Python jobs in `ci-python.yml`, including their `windows checks passed` and `python checks passed` verdicts; Linux jobs in `ci.yml` report `all checks passed`. These workflows remain manual-only in this fork. Preserve their shared concurrency and Node environment, the existing per-platform switches (`selfhosted` for in-house runners and `blacksmith` for hosted runners), Dependabot fallbacks, and reusable Python runtime platform inputs. Master platform checks, Wine, self-hosted standbys, and manual runner benchmarks remain in `ci-master.yml` ([platform policy](workflows/ci-master.yml), [failover runbook](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-ci-failover-runbook.md)).

The manual [Windows packaging workflow](workflows/windows-package.yml) uses the dedicated self-hosted Windows x64 label `dsh-win-package-trial` under native `pwsh`; preserve this routing separately from the automatic CI lanes.

The merge checks run from three workflows named `Policy`, which run on `pull_request_target` and cover pull requests into master or a `release/dsh-x.y.z` branch, so their definitions come from the base branch, and call the `deepseek-harness-check` action directly: `pr-check-on-head-branch.yml` on pull-request updates gives `Policy / Master Change` and `Policy / Pre-Merge Check`, `pr-check-after-approve.yml` on pull-request updates and submitted or dismissed reviews gives `Policy / Approve Check`, which also publishes the review verdict as the check run `Policy / Reviewer Check`, and `pr-check-on-base-branch.yml` on pushes to master or a release branch re-runs the head-branch checks as `Policy / Recheck`. Branch rules require those check names, so keep the job names and the workflow name. Each job reads its mode from a repository variable: `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF`, `MERGE_POLICY_PRE_MERGE`, and `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF`, each `off` (skip), `report` (run without failing the job), or `block` (fail the job); a missing value or an unknown one counts as `report`. `MERGE_POLICY_HEAD_DIFF` decides whether `Policy / Approve Check` runs and fails; while it runs, `Policy / Reviewer Check` is published whatever that mode says, with `success` when every file that needs review has one and `action_required` with the reviewers to ask otherwise. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` merges the commit `Policy / Master Change` reports, so it runs only after that job and stays off while `MERGE_POLICY_MASTER_DIFF` is `off`; a merge it cannot do and a build that fails both follow its own mode, so `report` warns and skips the build while `block` fails the job. `Policy / Pre-Merge Check` runs `scripts/pre-merge-check.ts` under plain Node and knows nothing else about the merged tree: that script checks the released manifests against the root version, installs, and builds the Host and Client contracts, so change it in one pull request together with the build it orchestrates. In this fork all three workflows are dispatch-only, so the event triggers and branch rules above apply only to the upstream repository.

The manual Desktop publication workflow selects the original successful `package` job attempt independently of `upload-artifact` archival status, then routes each retained build through `DESKTOP_PUBLISH_RUNNERS` to its original machine's unique label. Keep Windows run steps on native PowerShell and Mac run steps on the default POSIX shell; shared entrypoints are Node scripts. Test and production jobs use separate `desktop-test` and `desktop-production` approval Environments after a credential-free preparation job.
